title: Resilience Rendezvous — Ops Sprint Notes & Cross-Team Cohesion Experiments
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc captures a focused set of small, time-boxed experiments aimed at improving cross-team cohesion for SLO ownership and faster operational response across the inference stack. These are intentionally low-friction changes we can validate in a 6‑week sprint, with clear hypotheses and observable metrics.

Why this feels different from previous SLO docs:
- Prior artifacts mainly framed SLOs as static contracts. This experiment slate treats SLOs as behavioral levers — changing rituals, onboarding flows, and lightweight automation — to see whether team behavior (not just dashboards) reduces customer impact.
- Emphasis on short, measurable experiments with rollback plans so we can iterate quickly.

Goals (primary + secondary):
- Primary: Reduce customer-visible error budget burn incidents by 30% in targeted services over 6 weeks.
- Secondary: Cut mean time to action (MTA) for critical alerts by 40% for services in cohort A. Improve cross-team incident trust (measured via weekly post-incident 2-question pulse) from baseline ~2.4/5 to >=3.5/5.

Cohorts and scope:
- Cohort A (pilot): embedding-service, chat-router, kv-cache (three services spanning infra, runtime, and platform)
- Cohort B (observability only): dedicated pools controller, routing-policy-service
- Excluded: newly onboarded services and systems in active re-architecture (we want stable baselines)

Experiments (6 total, ranked):
1) Shared Incident Warm-handoff (2-week trial)
- Hypothesis: A 10-minute live warm-handoff at incident close between feature owners and SRE reduces recurrence and clarifies next steps.
- Runbook change: mandatory 10-minute "warm-handoff" step in incident close checklist for Cohort A services.
- Success metric: percent of incidents with documented corrective action in 48h increases from 58% -> 85%.
- Rollback: revert runbook enforcement if on-call time increases >15% or incident closure latency >20%.

2) SLO Pairing Rota (4-week trial)
- Hypothesis: Pairing one SRE and one product/feature engineer weekly for a focused SLO review reduces surprises and aligns alert thresholds.
- Implementation: lightweight 1-hour pairing slot + shared notes (template in Confluence).
- Success metric: reduction in alert-to-action time by 40% for paired teams.

3) Incident Micro-Playbook Cards (3-week trial)
- Hypothesis: 3-card micro-playbooks (network, memory pressure, token-flood) pinned in the Slack incident channel reduce cognitive load and speed triage.
- Implementation: create 3 one-page cards per service; bots surface the top card per alert.
- Success metric: first remediation action taken within 12 minutes for applicable alerts rises from baseline 45% -> 75%.

4) Error Budget Steering Signals (6-week trial)
- Hypothesis: Lightweight steering (weekly 10-minute "budget standup") prevents budget cliff events by making small course-corrections earlier.
- Implementation: auto-generated digest + 10-min slot on Friday ops sync for Cohort A.
- Success metric: zero budget cliff weeks (where burn-rate > 4x) for Cohort A across trial.

5) Prefix/KV Cache Canary (A/B config) (6-week trial)
- Hypothesis: Gradually enabling prefix cache sharing for a small percentage of traffic reduces p90 latency without increasing error rate.
- Implementation: rollout 10% -> 25% traffic using feature-flagged config with tight monitoring.
- Success metric: p90 latency drop >=8% with error rate delta <= 0.05%.

6) Cross-Team Blameless Retro Template (ongoing)
- Hypothesis: A concise retro template focusing on decisions, action owners, and acceptance criteria increases follow-through.
- Implementation: two-slide retro template + action register visible in Confluence.
- Success metric: closure rate of action items within 14 days increases to >=70%.

Milestones and timeline (6-week sprint):
- Week 0 (planning): finalize checklists, templates, runbook snippets. Owners assigned.
- Week 1–2: deploy Incident Warm-handoff and Micro-Playbook Cards. Start SLO Pairing rota.
- Week 3–4: begin Error Budget Steering signal digest, start cache canary at 10%.
- Week 5–6: expand cache canary to 25% if safe. Collect metrics, run cross-team retro, decide on wider rollout.

Roles & owners (single line per role):
- Program lead: Aisha Patel (eng-sre) — overall coordinator and decision owner for rollbacks.
- Runtime owner: Lucas Chen (serving-runtime) — cache canary, latency validation.
- Platform owner: Priya Singh (platform-engineering) — error budget digest, routing knobs.
- Observability lead: Marta Novak (observability) — dashboards, alert thresholds, automation for digests.
- Incident playbook author: Diego Alvarez (site-reliability-engineering) — micro-playbooks and runbook edits.
- Product liaison: Evan Brooks (product-hosted-api) — pairing rota and feature owner communication.

Communication plan (short):
- Daily stand: 15-min sync M–F during W1–W2 for experiment owners (standup channel: #resilience-rendezvous).
- Weekly ops show-and-tell: 30-min Friday summary with metrics spotlight.
- Slack bot digest: nightly error budget summary to #resilience-rendezvous and service-specific channels.

Metrics & data collection (how we’ll measure):
- Primary telemetry sources: Datadog SLO dashboards, internal metrics (burn-rate, p50/p90/p99 latency), and incident tracker (Jira REL-xxxx entries).
- Baseline capture window: previous 8 weeks for each metric.
- Reporting cadence: daily automated snapshots; weekly aggregated report for sprint review.

Risks and mitigations (short list):
- Increased on-call churn: monitor on-call load; if weekly average > +20% restore previous cadence.
- False positives from canary: conservative rollback thresholds and automated traffic shift to 0% on error rate spike.
- Ownership confusion: require pair sign-off on changes and update service README with contact matrix.

Runbook/automation changes (concrete):
- Add "warm-handoff" checklist step to incident close template (Confluence runbook id linked).
- Implement Slack bot that surfaces micro-playbook card per alert type.
- Generate weekly error budget digest automatically from SLO API and post to channels.

Acceptance criteria for success (go/no-go at sprint end):
- Data-driven: at least 3 of the 5 quantitative success metrics reached for Cohort A.
- Behavioral: >70% of pairing slots completed and documented notes present.
- Safety: no customer-impacting regression (>= P1 errors) attributable to experiments.

If success: prepare a 2-week follow-up to widen Cohort and bake the winning rituals into permanent runbooks and onboarding.
If partial success: keep high-signal experiments and iterate on low-signal ones with updated hypotheses.
If failure or safety incidents: execute rollback plan and run postmortem focused on experiment design failure modes.

Open questions / things to decide (short list):
- How do we track the "trust" metric in a lightweight, non-burdensome way? Proposal: two-question pulse after every incident for participants only.
- Who owns the long-term maintenance of micro-playbook cards (suggest Observability team).
- Should pairing be compensated as "collab hours" on calendars? Ops to decide with managers.

Notes to self / rough next steps (developer-style):
- Draft micro-playbook templates and post to Confluence draft space by Fri.
- Lucas to instrument canary flag and a rollback hook in the runtime by Tue.
- Marta to wire the digest and validation tests for false positives by Wed.
- Priya & Evan to schedule pairing slots and invite the first cohort of feature engineers.

Appendix — quick templates (pasted inline):
- Warm-handoff checklist (mini): incident summary, actions taken, unresolved risks, 48h owner assignment, next review date.
- Pairing note template: date, participants, SLO(s) reviewed, thresholds proposed, action owner with acceptance criteria.
- Micro-playbook card format: one-line symptom, 3 quick checks, one safe mitigation, telemetry to watch, follow-up owner.

This is intentionally concise; we will expand into separate living Confluence pages if the pilot yields signal. For now, use this doc as the single-source plan and coordination hub for the 6-week trial.

-- Aisha (notes updated 2026-03-12)
